How it works:
- **First line, `/* /* */`:** Rust allows comments inside comments, so for Rust a comment is still open after this line. C++ doesn't, so for C++ the comment ends on that same line. The C++ program that follows is therefore only visible to C++.
- **`// */` after the C++ code:** C++ treats this as an ordinary line comment. Rust is still inside its open comment, where `//` means nothing, so the `*/` closes that comment.
- **Rust code:** every line ends with `// \`. In C++, a backslash at the end of a `//` comment carries the comment onto the next line, so C++ reads the whole Rust part as one long comment. Rust sees normal code with a comment at the end of each line.
